```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(here)

devtools::load_all(debug = FALSE, recompile = TRUE)
library(dplyr)

library(readr)

stopifnot(params$n_replications >= 1, params$initial_population >= 2,
          params$years > params$burn_in, params$burn_in >= 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: functions

run_replication <- function(replication, model, grouped = FALSE) {
  set.seed(410000L + replication)
  population <- if (grouped) {
    create_baseline_population(params$initial_population, 50, 2000, group_weights = c(A = 1, B = 1))
  } else {
      create_baseline_population(params$initial_population, 50, 2000)
    }
  model <- model |> set_population(population)
  time <- system.time(result <- simulate(model, params$years, 420000L + replication))[["elapsed"]]
  result$runtime <- time
  return(result)
}
```

# Purpose and scope

This report assesses milestone 4: union dissolution, remarriage, and the
cohabitation stretch goal. It is a draft for scientific review, not a declaration
that the milestone has passed. The code adapts `milestone4_tests.R` to the current
interfaces; that working script is preserved separately.

| Mechanism | Demonstration | Quantity to inspect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dissolution | Shared rates, symmetric pair multipliers, explicit pair schedules | Dissolutions per union-year by elapsed duration |
| Remarriage | Age schedules by prior union; mixed age/duration schedules | Women's successful partnership entries per unpartnered year |
| Cohabitation | Type probabilities, separate matching, typed fertility and dissolution | Entry types, fertility, breakups, and available-partner histories |
| Conversion | Duration and woman's-age schedules | Conversions per cohabitation union-year |
| History and measurement | Linked conversion episodes; previous-category policy | Exact links, accounting, and distinct observation denominators |
| Matching | Separate cohabitation and marriage preferences | Conditional-choice recovery, rather than pooled cross-tab equality |

Dissolution and conversion inputs are annual hazards. Search inputs schedule
women's attempts, not men's transitions. Successful female union-entry rates
can be lower than search rates if attempts fail. Men's realized rates need not
match the female input schedule. No numerical scientific acceptance threshold
is prescribed here.

**Author assessment:** _Add interpretation of the results and any acceptance
criteria before closing the milestone._

# Overview of design


| Helper | Events | Exposure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `calculate_union_rates()` | Direct marriage plus cohabitation entry | Unpartnered years |
| `calculate_union_rates(by_union_type = TRUE)` | Each direct entry type separately | Same unpartnered years repeated for each type |
| `calculate_marriage_rates()` | Direct marriage plus conversion | Unpartnered plus cohabiting years |
| `calculate_dissolution_rates()` | Dissolution | Union-years of the selected type, or pooled |
| `calculate_cohab_convert_rate()` | Conversion | Cohabitation union-years |
| `calculate_demog_rates(by_union_type = TRUE)` | Births and deaths | Person-years by current type; no overall row |

# Inputs and replication design

## Rates and provenance

The local US fertility and marriage files are documented in
[data/usa_2000_rates.README.md](data/usa_2000_rates.README.md). Their calendar
years and denominators differ; these are demonstrations, not a fitted coherent
US population. The marriage file uses a direct-rate approximation to published
annual transitions. Reusing legal-marital fertility as partnership fertility
is also a modeling choice, not empirical evidence about cohabitation.

There is no checked-in US mortality table. The default below is explicitly
**illustrative mortality**, so the report renders without credentials or network
access. To use empirical mortality, save a validated table locally and supply
`mortality_file` as a project-relative path. All scenarios in one render use the
same mortality table. The following optional preparation step is not executed:


```{r}
#| label: input-rates

mortality_rates <- get_mortality_hmd("USA", year = 2000)

fertility_rates <- read_csv(
  here("validation", "data", "usa_2000_fertility_by_union_status.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  rename(union_type = union_status)
fertility_rates_typed <- bind_rows(
  filter(fertility_rates, union_type == "unpartnered"),
  filter(fertility_rates, union_type == "partnered") |>
    mutate(union_type = "marriage"),
  filter(fertility_rates, union_type == "partnered") |>
    mutate(union_type = "cohab", rate = rate * 0.5)
)

marriage_rates <- read_csv(
  here("validation", "data", "usa_2001_marriage_rates_female.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
marriage_rates_typed_age <- bind_rows(
  mutate(marriage_rates, previous_union = "none"),
  mutate(marriage_rates, previous_union = "dissolved", rate = rate * 1.1),
  mutate(marriage_rates, previous_union = "widowed", rate = rate * 0.9)
)
marriage_rates_typed_dur <- bind_rows(
  mutate(marriage_rates, previous_union = "none"),
  tibble(
    previous_union = "dissolved",
    dur_start = c(0, 1, 5, 15),
    dur_end = c(1, 5, 15, Inf),
    rate = c(.005, .04, .07, .01)
  ),
  tibble(
    previous_union = "widowed",
    dur_start = c(0, 1, 5, 15),
    dur_end = c(1, 5, 15, Inf),
    rate = c(.005, .06, .03, .01)
  )
)

dissolution_rates <- tibble(
  dur_start = c(0, 5, 10, 15),
  dur_end = c(5, 10, 15, 20),
  rate = -log(c(.80, .68, .60, .52) / c(1, .80, .68, .60)) / 5
)
dissolution_rates_typed <- bind_rows(
  mutate(dissolution_rates, union_type = "cohab", rate = rate * 2),
  mutate(dissolution_rates, union_type = "marriage")
)

cohab_probability <- tibble(
  age_start = c(15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40),
  age_end = c(20, 25, 30, 35, 40, Inf),
  prob = c(.4, .25, .15, .1, .05, .01)
)

conversion_rates_dur <- tibble(
  dur_start = c(0, 5, 10),
  dur_end = c(5, 10, Inf),
  rate = c(.15, .30, .05)
)
conversion_rates_age <- tibble(
  age_start = c(15, 25, 35, 50),
  age_end = c(25, 35, 50, Inf),
  rate = c(.08, .18, .25, .10)
)

time_breaks <- c(2000 + params$burn_in, 2000 + params$years)
time_scenario <- tibble(scenario = character(), elapsed_time = double())
```

The dissolution schedule follows the numerical illustration in the working test
script: successive five-year survival proportions of .80, .68, .60, and .52
are converted to piecewise-constant hazards. These values are retained as an
**illustration**, not independently verified estimates from the NSFG. The
schedule ends at duration 20; subsequent dissolution hazard is zero. The
remarriage multipliers, duration schedules, cohabitation probabilities, typed
fertility modifications, and conversion hazards below are all illustrative.

## Initialization, observation, and Monte Carlo uncertainty

Each replication generates its own starting population, with maximum starting
age 50, and uses a separate simulation seed. This incorporates starting-population
variation into the Monte Carlo uncertainty. The same population seed is reused
across scenarios for a replication; scenarios are therefore paired, although
results below describe each scenario separately. Equal simulation seeds do not
preserve event-by-event coupling when mechanisms change random-number use.

Runs are sequential and reduced to summary tables immediately, so full histories
are not retained across replications. Increase `n_replications` for final analysis;
ten is an exploratory default. The first `burn_in` years are excluded from rate
measurement; this does not establish that the population has reached stability.
Sparse cells, especially young widows, can remain noisy after pooling periods.

Means and MCSEs are calculated from replication-specific rates, not individual
unions or births. Each table reports the number of finite replication estimates;
zero-exposure rates are NA and omitted from the mean, so sparse-cell means are
conditional on positive exposure. Pooled event/exposure rates are displayed
separately. Neither measure is a confidence interval for empirical parameters.



# Duration-dependent dissolution

## Basic dissolution rates

```{r}
#| label: run-simulations-basic-dissolution
model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_mortality(mortality_rates) |>
  set_fertility(fertility_rates) |>
  set_union_formation("rate", rates = marriage_rates) |>
  set_union_dissolution(dissolution_rates)

results <- map(seq_len(params$n_replications), run_replication, model = model)

time_scenario <- bind_rows(
  time_scenario,
  tibble(
    scenario = "basic dissolution",
    elapsed_time = mean(map_dbl(results, function(x) {x$runtime}))
  )
)

dissolution_by_rep <- results |>
  map(
    calculate_dissolution_rates,
    time_breaks = time_breaks,
    dur_breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 15, 20)
  ) |>
  bind_rows(.id = "replication")

dissolution_summary <- dissolution_by_rep |>
  group_by(time_start, time_end, dur_start, dur_end) |>
  summarize(
    n_valid = sum(!is.na(rate_dissolution)),
    rate_mean = if (n_valid > 0) {
      mean(rate_dissolution, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else NA_real_,
    rate_mcse = if (n_valid > 1) {
      sd(rate_dissolution, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n_valid)
    } else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-basic-dissolution-rates
#| fig-cap: Comparison of mean union dissolution rate by duration across simulations. 95% confidence intervals are shown. Dotted line shows the input dissolution rate.

dissolution_summary |>
  filter(dur_start < 20) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dur_start + 2.5, y = rate_mean))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = rate_mean - 1.96 * rate_mcse, ymax = rate_mean + 1.96 * rate_mcse))+
  geom_line(data = dissolution_rates, aes(y = rate), linetype = 2)+
  labs(x = "union duration", y = "dissolution rate")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-basic-dissolution-rates
#| tbl-cap: Mean union dissolution rates by duration across simulations with Monte Carlo standard errors and the target input dissolution rates.

dissolution_summary |>
  left_join(dissolution_rates, by = c("dur_start", "dur_end")) |>
  filter(dur_start < 20) |>
  select(-starts_with("time_")) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    dur_start ~ "Dur. start",
    dur_end ~ "Dur. end",
    n_valid ~ "Valid cases",
    rate_mean ~ "Mean rate",
    rate_mcse ~ "MCSE",
    rate ~ "Target rate"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(c("rate_mean", "rate"), decimals = 4) |>
  fmt_number("rate_mcse", decimals = 5)
```

@fig-basic-dissolution-rates and @tbl-basic-dissolution-rates show the mean duration-specific dissolution rates observed across the simulations with a reported Monte Carlo standard error. These simulations have no groups and no adjustment for cohabitation or remarriage. The input dissolution rates are shown for comparison. The results are extremeley close to the input dissolution rates and well within the 95% confidence intervals.

## Group-pairing-specific dissolution rates

To test group differences in the dissolution rate, I use a two group simulation where intergroup unions (i.e. A:B) have 10% higher dissolution rates than intragroup unions.

```{r}
#| label: run-simulations-grouped-dissolution

dissolution_rates_grouped <- bind_rows(
  mutate(dissolution_rates, group_pair = "A:A"),
  mutate(dissolution_rates, group_pair = "A:B", rate = rate * 1.1),
  mutate(dissolution_rates, group_pair = "B:B")
)

model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_mortality(mortality_rates) |>
  set_fertility(fertility_rates) |>
  set_union_formation("rate", rates = marriage_rates) |>
  set_union_dissolution(dissolution_rates_grouped)

results <- map(seq_len(params$n_replications), run_replication, model = model, grouped = TRUE)

time_scenario <- bind_rows(
  time_scenario,
  tibble(
    scenario = "grouped dissolution",
    elapsed_time = mean(map_dbl(results, function(x) {x$runtime}))
  )
)

dissolution_by_rep <- results |>
  map(
    calculate_dissolution_rates,
    time_breaks = time_breaks,
    dur_breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 15, 20),
    by_group = TRUE
  ) |>
  bind_rows(.id = "replication")

dissolution_summary <- dissolution_by_rep |>
  group_by(time_start, time_end, dur_start, dur_end, group_pair) |>
  summarize(
    n_valid = sum(!is.na(rate_dissolution)),
    rate_mean = if (n_valid > 0) {
      mean(rate_dissolution, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else NA_real_,
    rate_mcse = if (n_valid > 1) {
      sd(rate_dissolution, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n_valid)
    } else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-grouped-dissolution-rates
#| fig-cap: Comparison of mean union dissolution rate by duration and group across simulations. 95% confidence intervals are shown. Dotted line shows the input dissolution rate.

dissolution_summary |>
  filter(dur_start < 20) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dur_start + 2.5, y = rate_mean, group = group_pair, color = group_pair))+
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7)+
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = rate_mean - 1.96 * rate_mcse, ymax = rate_mean + 1.96 * rate_mcse), alpha = 0.7)+
  geom_line(data = dissolution_rates_grouped, aes(y = rate), linetype = 2, alpha = 0.7)+
  labs(x = "union duration", y = "dissolution rate")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-grouped-dissolution-rates
#| tbl-cap: Mean union dissolution rates by duration and group across simulations with Monte Carlo standard errors and the target input dissolution rates.

dissolution_summary |>
  left_join(dissolution_rates_grouped, by = c("dur_start", "dur_end", "group_pair")) |>
  filter(dur_start < 20) |>
  select(-starts_with("time_")) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    dur_start ~ "Dur. start",
    dur_end ~ "Dur. end",
    group_pair ~ "Group pairing",
    n_valid ~ "Valid cases",
    rate_mean ~ "Mean rate",
    rate_mcse ~ "MCSE",
    rate ~ "Target rate"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(c("rate_mean", "rate"), decimals = 4) |>
  fmt_number("rate_mcse", decimals = 5)
```

@fig-grouped-dissolution-rates and @tbl-grouped-dissolution-rates show the mean duration-specific dissolution rates by group pairing observed across the simulations with a reported Monte Carlo standard error. These simulations have two  groups and no adjustment for cohabitation or remarriage or otheer group differences in input rates. The input dissolution rates are shown for comparison. The results are extremeley close to the input dissolution rates and well within the 95% confidence intervals.

## Duration-specific marraiage rate schedules for remarriages

The `none` schedule remains age-specific. The other categories use time since
the latest actual ending. Providing `dur_breaks` automatically separates prior
categories. Do not compare a broad age average with a duration hazard.

```{r}
#| label: duration-remarriage-recovery
union_summary |>
  filter(scenario == "remarriage_duration", sex == "f", previous_union != "none",
         is.finite(dur_end)) |>
  ggplot(aes((dur_start + dur_end) / 2, mean, color = previous_union, group = previous_union)) +
  geom_point() + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - 1.96 * mcse, ymax = mean + 1.96 * mcse), width = .25) +
  geom_line(data = search_duration |> filter(previous_union != "none", is.finite(dur_end)),
    aes(y = rate), linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Years since latest ending", y = "Successful union entries per unpartnered year")
```

```{r}
#| label: never-partnered-recovery
union_summary |>
  filter(scenario == "remarriage_duration", sex == "f", previous_union == "none", age_start < 70) |>
  ggplot(aes(age_start + 2.5, mean)) + geom_point() +
  geom_line(data = search_base |> filter(age_start < 70), aes(y = rate), linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Woman's age", y = "Successful union entries per unpartnered year")
```

# Cohabitation

A search first selects intended type using `cohab_prob`, then applies that
type's matching preferences. Failure does not form an episode. Cohabitors remain
unavailable for new partnerships. Conversion closes the cohabitation and starts
a marriage with the same partners, linked by `previous_cohab_id`; dissolution
duration resets. Exact ties execute death, birth, dissolution, conversion, search.


Repeated union-entry exposure must not be summed across the two type rows.
Marriage rates including conversion are not expected to equal the female search
schedule. Births tied to conversion retain cohabitation type; deaths use the
left-limit type. These boundary rules have exact unit tests in addition to the
replicated demonstrations here.

```{r}
#| label: history-invariants
measurements$checks |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarize(across(c(valid_links, all_conversions_linked, exclusive_partners), all), .groups = "drop") |>
  gt()
stopifnot(all(measurements$checks$valid_links),
          all(measurements$checks$all_conversions_linked),
          all(measurements$checks$exclusive_partners))
```

```{r}
#| label: episode-endings
measurements$endings |>
  group_by(scenario, union_type, end_reason) |>
  summarize(episodes = sum(episodes), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(startsWith(scenario, "cohab")) |>
  gt() |> sub_missing(columns = end_reason, missing_text = "Ongoing")
```

## Pooled union formation with cohabitation

Pooled female entries should track the overall search hazard when matching
succeeds. High cohabitation probability alone should not reduce this pooled
rate. Type-specific intensities are lambda*p and lambda*(1-p); coarse averages
require exposure weighting, especially if probabilities vary by age, group or
prior category. Pooled cross-tab ratios do not isolate matching parameters.

```{r}
#| label: cohab-pooled-search
union_summary |>
  filter(scenario == "cohab_duration", sex == "f", age_start < 70) |>
  ggplot(aes(age_start + 2.5, mean, color = previous_union, group = previous_union)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line() + facet_wrap(~ group) +
  geom_line(data = search_age |> filter(age_start < 70), aes(y = rate), linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Woman's age", y = "Pooled union entries per unpartnered year")
```

```{r}
#| label: cohab-entry-type-rates
summarize_rate(measurements$union_type, "rate_union", "person_years", "unions") |>
  filter(scenario == "cohab_duration", sex == "f", age_start < 70) |>
  ggplot(aes(age_start + 2.5, mean, color = union_type, group = union_type)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line() + facet_grid(previous_union ~ group) +
  labs(x = "Woman's age", y = "Type-specific entries per unpartnered year")
```

## Type-specific fertility and dissolution

The typed fertility multiplier-list interface also accepts
`list(unpartnered = c(B = 1.1), cohab = c(B = 1.2), marriage = c(B = .9))`.
With shared partnered schedules the corresponding key is `partnered`.
This report keeps multipliers at one; exact multiplier equivalence is covered
by the software tests. Fertility compensation is based on current input bands,
not the complete past sequence of union-type transitions, so perfect recovery
of typed fertility is not guaranteed (D045).

```{r}
#| label: typed-fertility
summarize_rate(measurements$demog, "rate_fertility", "person_years", "births") |>
  filter(scenario == "cohab_duration", sex == "f", age_start < 45) |>
  ggplot(aes(age_start + 2.5, mean, color = union_type, group = union_type)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line() + facet_wrap(~ group) +
  geom_line(data = fertility_typed, aes(y = rate), linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Woman's age", y = "Births per woman-year in current type")
```

```{r}
#| label: typed-dissolution
dissolution_summary |>
  filter(scenario == "cohab_duration", dur_start < 20) |>
  ggplot(aes(dur_start + 2.5, mean, color = union_type, group = union_type)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line() + facet_wrap(~ group_pair) +
  geom_line(data = dissolution_typed, aes(y = rate), linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Duration of current episode", y = "Dissolutions per union-year")
```

## Conversion hazard recovery

Conversion is measured directly over cohabitation exposure. Dissolution and
partner death stop exposure but do not enter the conversion numerator.

```{r}

conversion_summary |>

  ggplot(aes(dur_start, mean, color = group, group = group)) +
  geom_point() + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - 1.96 * mcse, ymax = mean + 1.96 * mcse), width = .2) +
  geom_line(data = conversion_duration, inherit.aes = FALSE,
    mapping = aes(x = dur_start, y = rate), linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Cohabitation duration band start", y = "Conversions per cohabitation union-year")
```

```{r}
#| label: age-conversion
conversion_summary |>
  filter(scenario == "cohab_age") |>
  ggplot(aes(age_start, mean, color = group, group = group)) +
  geom_point() + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - 1.96 * mcse, ymax = mean + 1.96 * mcse), width = .2) +
  geom_line(data = conversion_age, mapping = aes(x = age_start, y = rate),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, linetype = 2) +
```

## Prior-category policy and marriage observation

By default a cohabitation ending restores the category from earlier legal
marriages: someone with no marriage history returns to `none`. With
`cohabitation_counts_as_previous_union = TRUE`, cohabitation breakup/death
counts as dissolved/widowed. Exposure during cohabitation and the subsequent
conversion retain the category held before entry. The policy changes who is
eligible for each prior-category search schedule; output population composition
can therefore differ. These are two definitions, not competing estimates of the
same parameter.

```{r}
#| label: previous-policy-comparison
measurements$union |>
  filter(scenario %in% c("cohab_duration", "cohab_previous_policy"), sex == "f") |>
  group_by(scenario, previous_union) |>
  summarize(person_years = sum(person_years), entries = sum(unions), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(pooled_rate = entries / person_years) |> gt()
```

```{r}
#| label: marriages-including-conversion
summarize_rate(measurements$marriage, "rate_marriage", "person_years", "marriages") |>
  filter(scenario == "cohab_duration", sex == "f", age_start < 70) |>
  ggplot(aes(age_start + 2.5, mean, color = previous_union, group = previous_union)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line() + facet_wrap(~ group) +
  labs(x = "Woman's age", y = "Marriage entries per nonmarried year (including conversion)")
```

**Author assessment:** _Discuss pooled search recovery, typed fertility and
breakups, both conversion clocks, and the prior-category policy._

# Matching parameter recovery

The separate offline recovery script fits conditional-choice models with the
recorded group-weight offsets, attained-age terms and available male choice
sets. Conversion-created marriage episodes are excluded because no partner
choice occurs at conversion. Both types exclude partnered men from alternatives.
Its synthetic inputs differ from the empirical/illustrative scenarios above.

The table below reads the previously generated evidence, rather than silently
rerunning it or treating pooled cross-tabs as exact constraints. Its ten
independent starting populations and estimated MCSEs are documented in
[the testing record](../docs/testing.md). To regenerate with the current source,
run this separately from the repository root:

```{r}
#| label: matching-regeneration-command
#| eval: false
# Uses the current optimized development build; writes replication estimates,
# a summary and source/session metadata. No rate downloads.
system2("Rscript", c("validation/validate-cohabitation-matching.R", "dev",
                    "validation/cohabitation-matching", "10"))
```

```{r}
#| label: recorded-matching-evidence
matching_file <- here("validation", "cohabitation-matching-summary.csv")
if (file.exists(matching_file)) {
  read_csv(matching_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    filter(parameter == "log_odds") |>
    mutate(target = if_else(union_type == "cohab", -2, -6)) |>
    gt() |> fmt_number(columns = c(mean, mcse, target), decimals = 4)
} else cat("Recorded recovery evidence is absent; run the script above.")
```

**Author assessment:** _Review the saved evidence's source/session metadata and
rerun as needed before final acceptance. Do not infer directional symmetry or
exact pooled cross-tab odds from conditional-choice recovery alone._

# Performance, reproducibility, and limitations

```{r}
#| label: observed-runtime
measurements$timing |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarize(replications = n(), mean_seconds = mean(elapsed),
            min_seconds = min(elapsed), max_seconds = max(elapsed), .groups = "drop") |>
  gt() |> fmt_number(columns = ends_with("seconds"), decimals = 3)
```

These are wall times for this render, not a controlled benchmark against the
pre-milestone engine. Use an installed optimized build or
`devtools::load_all(debug = FALSE)` for timing; debug compilation can inflate
runtime substantially. Rates are summarized after each run and histories are
released. Serial execution avoids holding several large populations in RAM.

Software checks are documented in [docs/testing.md](../docs/testing.md). Before
closeout, run the complete offline suite from the repository root:

```{r}
#| label: full-suite-command
#| eval: false
devtools::test()
```

Retained limitations include transition-aware fertility compensation, failed
searches in thin pools, initialization transients, approximate age/cohort bins
for calibration, and incomplete-history uncertainty. Cohabitation is rate-mode
only. Previous-marriage-order effects, richer couple covariates, and former-
partner/father continuity remain outside this milestone. This report does not
perform a new executable SOCSIM comparison; source audits and intentional
model differences are documented separately.
